requirements.title: Character literals have matching delimiters and an optional kind prefix
requirements.definition: A character literal uses a matching pair of apostrophes or a matching pair of quotation marks, surrounding zero or more rep-char occurrences. An optional kind-param precedes the opening delimiter and is separated from it by an underscore. R709 defines that prefix as a digit string or scalar integer constant name, not an arbitrary expression. C718/C719 and C732 retain their own name/type, sign and supported-method conditions. The source-form definition of rep-char and the doubling/empty-context rules below are part of interpreting this syntax.

In phase 2 only, serialize the default character kind from an independent inquiry without narrowing; materialize that digit token in two fixed fixtures and bind a profile to that exact default-kind value. A 64-decimal-digit construction bound must be established by repeated default-integer division, not by conversion into a supposedly wider selected kind. Different identifiers or a larger token make only these finite witnesses unavailable; 1/4/8 are never presumed. Check LEN, KIND and the default-kind value after admission.

The real candidate has the small value 1.0, not an arbitrary kind identifier converted to real. Require noninteger-name, nonconstant-name, nonscalar-name and prefix-grammar causes respectively. requirements.title: A literal kind prefix names a supported character method
requirements.definition: The literal's kind-param identifies an available character representation method. R709/C718/C719 independently constrain the prefix syntax, integer constant name and nonnegative value. A kind supported for another intrinsic type is not thereby a supported character kind.

pending.unsupported-nonnegative-prefix: Planned compile diagnoses C732_invalid__absent_zero_apostrophe and C732_invalid__absent_zero_quotation, each with its same-suffix C732_valid__absent_zero_apostrophe_repair or C732_valid__absent_zero_quotation_repair. An independent character-kind-zero-absent profile must establish 0 is absent from CHARACTER_KINDS; replace only prefix 0 with a declared supported dk. Require the literal's actual CHARACTER kind value 0/support cause. A negative prefix value would also violate C719 and is not used to isolate this condition.

requirements.oracle: An unprofiled run uses a supported named default kind prefix with both delimiters and checks literal kind, count and value. No unsupported-nonnegative-prefix case is authored without an independent absence profile. Direct case IDs: C732_valid__supported.
requirements.oracle_limitation: A processor that supports character kind zero makes the absent-zero witnesses unavailable, not passing. Generic kind/constant/expected messages, undefined-name reports, unsupported character-literal facilities and crashes do not establish the intended unsupported representation value. Reporting need not be fatal.

requirements.title: Literal kind comes from its prefix or the default method
requirements.definition: A supplied kind prefix determines the literal's character kind; without it the literal is default character. The prefix is not part of the literal value or its represented length. Prefix selection does not imply distinctness from default, optional-kind availability, byte width or a source encoding.

pending.selected-named-methods: Planned qualified runs S7_4_4_3_001_valid__ascii and S7_4_4_3_001_valid__iso10646: instantiate the respective selected kind only in separately profile-qualified files. The selected method may equal default, and unsupported names must not appear in declarations hidden behind runtime IF statements.

requirements.oracle: Two run programs inquire directly on empty and nonempty literals, with absent, KIND-derived and SELECTED_CHAR_KIND(DEFAULT)-derived named prefixes and both delimiters. They check exact kinds and lengths before assignment can convert or pad. Optional named/source-interface branches remain pending. Direct case IDs: S7_4_4_3_001_valid__default, S7_4_4_3_001_valid__named_prefix.

requirements.title: Literal repertoire is method-specific and source-form-specific
requirements.source: 7.4.4.3 p3 and its two bullets; PDF 85, printed 71, lines 37-41.
requirements.definition: rep-char is interpreted in the prefixed character method, or default character when no prefix is present. In free source form it is a graphic character in that processor-dependent set. In fixed form it can be any character in the corresponding set, but the processor may restrict some or all control characters. Extra graphics, controls, nondefault kinds and byte-to-character mappings are not universally required by this definition.

requirements.oracle: Separate free- and fixed-form run fixtures check a finite required-graphic subset with both literal delimiters, case distinction and exact interior/edge blanks. requirements.title: Delimiters are excluded while literal character data is preserved
requirements.source: 7.4.4.3 p4; PDF 85, printed 71, line 42, with p3's rep-char domain and canonical character-context premises.
requirements.definition: The surrounding delimiter pair is not part of a literal's value. Interior data, including a delimiter of the other kind, retains its character identity under the rep-char rules. Character-context case and blank exceptions remain operative; they do not permit folding letter case, collapsing interior blanks or counting delimiters in the represented length.

pending.case-and-blank-dependencies: Planned finite source/evidence connection to S6_1_2_002_valid__literals, S6_3_2_4_006_valid__raw_blanks at tests/fixtures/free_source_character_blanks/fixture.json, and S6_3_3_1_002_valid__character_blanks at tests/fixtures/fixed_source_1_002_valid_character_blanks/fixture.json. Preserve their paths, raw layout, individual oracles and primary owners. Before linking, check exact LEN as well as literal identity and retain the case-distinctness assertions; equality alone can hide folding or blank padding. No lexical metadata or existing source is changed now.

requirements.oracle: Three run programs check literal lengths 0/1/3 directly and verify nonempty positions. Opposite delimiters occur undoubled as data, are checked against one-character literals and are required to be distinct. Canonical case/blank evidence links remain pending. Direct case IDs: S7_4_4_3_003_valid__apostrophe, S7_4_4_3_003_valid__opposite_delimiters, S7_4_4_3_003_valid__quotation.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No negative program follows from excluding delimiters or preserving data. Literal equality with an identically misprocessed literal is not enough: counts and distinct-value contrasts are required. This finite plan is neither exhaustive decoding nor typography evidence.

requirements.title: A doubled matching delimiter represents one character
requirements.definition: Inside an apostrophe-delimited literal, two immediately consecutive apostrophes denote one apostrophe value. Inside a quotation-delimited literal, two immediately consecutive quotation marks denote one quotation-mark value. No intervening blank is part of the doubling spelling, and each doubled pair contributes one character to LEN, not two. The other delimiter does not require doubling just because it is punctuation.
requirements.oracle: Three run programs check each matching-delimiter doubling, including boundary and repeated pairs, using represented counts 3 and 2 and opposite-delimiter identity controls. The generator preserves exact source quote bytes; no backslash-escape extension is assumed. Direct case IDs: S7_4_4_3_004_valid__apostrophe, S7_4_4_3_004_valid__boundaries, S7_4_4_3_004_valid__quotation.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No artificial invalid twin is added for this value effect. A separated pair would enter other token/grammar rules and is not a new mandatory rejection oracle under this S ID. No backslash escape extension is assumed.
requirements.dependencies: R724 and p3-p4/p6 (PDF 85-86); 3.21 (PDF 21); 9.4.1 and 16.9.122 (PDF 151, 426). NOTE 1 is explanatory only and does not create another requirement.

requirements.title: An adjacent delimiter pair outside character context denotes an empty literal
requirements.definition: Two adjacent apostrophes, or two adjacent quotation marks, with no intervening blank and beginning outside a character context, denote a zero-length literal. A doubled delimiter within an already-open literal instead denotes delimiter data under p5. An empty literal is not the same length as a one-blank literal, even though padded character equality can consider their values equal.
requirements.oracle: Three run cases distinguish outside-context empty pairs, one-blank literals and inside-context doubled delimiter data by counts 0/1/1. Empty concatenation has unchanged value and count. Equality alone is not the empty-length oracle. Direct case IDs: S7_4_4_3_005_valid__apostrophe, S7_4_4_3_005_valid__context, S7_4_4_3_005_valid__quotation.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No negative or trapping behavior is inferred for an empty value. Runtime success would be a finite effect witness, not proof of every lexer context or source representation.
